title: Bi-Continuous W-Rich Refractory High Entropy Alloy-Cu Composite: Toward Material Innovation of Nuclear Reactor Coolant System.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: A W-rich refractory high-entropy alloy (likely bcc W–Nb–Mo–Ta or W–Nb–Mo–Ta–V) prepared as a porous scaffold, with high-purity Cu used as the infiltrant.
recollection.intervention: Guess: Fabrication of an interpenetrating (bi-continuous) composite by first forming a continuous, porous W-rich RHEA preform via powder metallurgy/sintering, then pressureless or vacuum pressure infiltration of molten Cu to fill the pore network; post-infiltration heat treatment to stabilize interfaces and tune volume fractions (e.g., 40–60 vol% Cu).
recollection.structure: Guess: A bi-continuous interpenetrating network consisting of a continuous bcc W-rich RHEA skeleton and a continuous fcc Cu phase, with a characteristic ligament/channel size on the order of 1–10 micrometers, clean interfaces with minimal intermetallic formation due to immiscibility, and stable microstructure under thermal cycling.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Synergistic load-sharing and heat transport: the W-rich RHEA skeleton provides high-temperature strength, creep resistance, and irradiation defect sink density (interfaces), while the continuous Cu network delivers high thermal/electrical conductivity and toughness. The bi-continuous geometry mitigates CTE mismatch stresses, improves thermal shock tolerance, and protects Cu from corrosive coolants via percolating RHEA pathways.
recollection.results: Guess: Room-temperature thermal conductivity ~180–220 W/m·K (retaining >150 W/m·K at 600 °C); RT tensile yield strength ~600–800 MPa (compressive yield ~1.2–1.5 GPa); retention of >300 MPa yield at 600 °C; fracture toughness in the 20–35 MPa·√m range; CTE ~9–11 ppm/K; electrical conductivity ~40–60% IACS. In liquid-metal coolant (e.g., LBE or Na) exposure at 450–550 °C, low mass-loss rates (on the order of a few mg/cm² after ~100–500 h) with limited Cu leaching due to the RHEA network. Under ion or surrogate irradiation, reduced swelling and helium bubble density relative to monolithic Cu, attributed to high interface sink strength. Intended for high-heat-flux coolant system components with improved strength–conductivity balance and corrosion/irradiation tolerance.

score.note: The recollection explicitly guesses an incorrect powder-metallurgy/infiltration route rather than liquid-metal dealloying of directionally solidified WTaVTi in molten Cu. It identifies continuous BCC RHEA and FCC Cu networks, but this largely follows the title and incorrectly proposes micrometer-scale channels and clean interfaces, missing the ~300 nm W-rich interlayer. The conductivity/load-sharing explanation is generic and misses preferential Ti–Cu exchange, W-rich passivation, and the reported temperature-dependent transport mechanism. Numerical conductivity estimates are far above the actual ~75 W m−1 K−1 at room temperature and ~120 W m−1 K−1 near 650 °C; most other quoted properties were not reported.
